'''''Tetraneuris scaposa''''' (common names '''stemmy four-nerve daisy'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TESC2|taxon=Tetraneuris scaposa|accessdate=9 December 2015}}</ref> and  '''stemmy hymenoxys''') is a North American species of flowering plant in the [[Asteraceae|sunflower family]]. It is native to the southwestern and south-central United States ([[Nebraska]], [[Kansas]], [[Oklahoma]], [[Texas]], [[New Mexico]], [[Arizona]], [[Utah]], and [[Colorado]]) and northern Mexico ([[Chihuahua (state)|Chihuahua]], [[Coahuila]], [[Nuevo León]], [[Tamaulipas]], [[San Luis Potosí]], and [[Zacatecas]]).<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Tetraneuris%20scaposa.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref>Turner, B. L. 2013. The comps of Mexico. A systematic account of the family Asteraceae (chapter 11: tribe Helenieae). Phytologia Memoirs 16: 1–100</ref><ref>[http://swbiodiversity.org/seinet/taxa/index.php?taxon=18807&taxauthid=1 SEINet Southwestern Biodiversity, Arizona chapter] description, photos, distribution map</ref>

''Tetraneuris scaposa'' is a perennial herb up to 40 cm (16 inches) tall. It forms a branching underground [[caudex]] sometimes producing as many as 100 above-ground stems. Leaves are concentrated low on the stem, close to the ground. Flower heads can either be present individually one per stem, or multiply in tight clumps. Each head has 12–26 ray flowers surrounding 25–180 disc flowers.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250067733 Flora of North America, ''Tetraneuris scaposa'' (de Candolle) Greene, 1898. ]</ref>

==Uses==
The [[Zuni people]] use an [[infusion]] of it as an [[eyewash]]. The [[Zuni people|Zuni]] believe that this eyewash is not for people with a "bad heart".<ref>Stevenson, Matilda Coxe 1915 Ethnobotany of the Zuni Indians. SI-BAE Annual Report #30 (p. 60, 61)</ref>
